cd /home/hyphyphyph/piton/repl; f=spec/ui/components/right-sidebar/tasks/index.pi; sed -i '262i\        - Time: where its time went, as its time breakdown says, once it has started' $f
cat >> $f <<'EOF'

    timeBreakdown:
        An open task that has started, and an open chain or step, has a Time
        section, beneath its Steps, or its Prompt where it has none, and
        above its Details, showing where its time went, so what is slow can
        be seen at a glance: waiting on the model, building the spec,
        running commands, and the rest.

        Its time is split into kinds, each with a colour of its own, drawn
        from the theme's chart colours, distinct from one another in light
        and dark mode and never a mode's colour, so a kind looks the same in
        every task:

        \\
        - Queued: waiting in its lane's queue before it was sent
        - Spec build: building the spec ahead of it, and after it for a spec step
        - Preparing: building or starting its container, and the snapshots taken as it started and ended
        - Model: the harness waiting on the model, thinking and writing, between tool calls
        - Commands: shell commands it ran and waited on, a build or tests among them
        - Files: reading, searching, and editing files
        - Subagents: subagents it waited on
        - Web: fetching and searching the web
        - Other: any other tool call, and time that fits none of these
        \\

        Each kind's time is worked out from the times its record keeps, as
        the @{ProjectData} says: each phase from its start to its end, and
        each tool call from when it was made to when its result came,
        counted as its kind; Model is the time between, from each turn's
        start, or a tool call's result, to the next tool call or the turn's
        end. A subagent's own tool calls count as Subagents, not as their own
        kinds, and background tasks that ran beside the main thread are
        never counted twice: only the time the task itself waited on them.
        Time while paused is left out, as is the gap between a chain's steps.

        Along the top of the section, a single bar, the section's full width
        and 12 pixels tall, with corners rounded 3 pixels, split into a
        segment per kind in the order above, each as wide as its share of
        the whole, a pixel of the section's surface between segments, kinds
        with no time left out. Beneath it, a legend, one line per kind with
        time, in order of the time it took, largest first: a square of its
        colour, its name, its time, as the @{MessageList} writes times, and
        its share, muted, as "Model 4:12 · 61%". The largest is in the
        theme's text colour and the rest muted, so what took longest stands
        out. Hovering a segment, or its legend line, lightens the other
        segments and shows a tooltip giving the kind's time, its share, and,
        for Commands, Files, Subagents, and Web, how many calls and the
        slowest of them, as "npm run build, 1:38".

        Beneath the legend, a timeline of the task from start to end, the
        section's full width and 24 pixels tall: each phase and tool call as
        a bar at its place along it, in its kind's colour, so long waits and
        when they came can be seen, with a muted time at either end. Hovering
        a bar names what it was and how long it took, and clicking a tool
        call's bar opens the task's output scrolled to that row.

        While the task runs, the section follows it, the kind under way
        growing in place and the timeline extending to now. A chain's Time
        section shows its steps' time together, the bar split by kind across
        all of them, and the timeline marking where each step began; each
        step's own section shows its own. A task from before its phases were
        kept shows only its total time, muted, saying its breakdown wasn't
        recorded.
EOF
grep -q "import ProjectData" $f || sed -i '0,/^from /s#^from #from /scope/project-data import ProjectData\nfrom #' $f; grep -q "import MessageList" $f; echo $?; piton check 2>&1|tail -2

content.text:
Opening a task, chain or step in the Tasks tab now shows a "Time" section breaking down where its time went. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 84 files.

- **Kinds of time:**
  - Queued, Spec build, Preparing (container and snapshots).
  - Model (waiting on the agent to think and write).
  - Commands (builds, tests, other shell commands), Files, Subagents, Web, Other.
  - Paused time and the gaps between a chain's steps aren't counted.
  - Background tasks only count for the time the task actually waited on them.
- **The chart:** a single stacked bar split by kind, with a legend beneath it ordered largest first, such as "Model 4:12 · 61%". The largest is highlighted. Hovering highlights a kind and shows its call count and slowest call, such as "npm run build, 1:38".
- **Timeline:** beneath the legend, every phase and tool call is placed along the task's duration. Clicking a tool call's bar jumps to that row in the output.
- **Live and chains:** it updates while the task runs. A chain shows all its steps together, with step boundaries marked.
- **Older tasks:** tasks recorded before phases were kept show only their total.
- **Theme:** I added a set of nine "chart colours" to the theme, distinct from the mode and status colours and readable in both light and dark mode.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `TasksTab` `#time-breakdown` and `#details`, `Theme` `#chart-colours`, and `ProjectData` `#contents` and `DebugLog` `#logged` for the phase times.
